task: Only focus on the reproduction of Fig. 1a-right panel (density distribution for P=0). The caption of the figure containing this subplot begins with 'On-site pair correlation xxx (left column)  of spin-up and spin-down ...'. You ONLY reproduce the density distributions (spin-up, spin-down, difference of these two, and non-interacting) of the (20, 20) case. You MUST use ITensors and ITensorMPS packages.

children.issue: The code plots the rescaled density distributions as a function of dimensionless coordinate ((i-i_{center})*2/L, where i is the site index).
The calculated density distributions must be rescaled (or multiplied) by the factor L/2, where L is the system size.
The code plots the density distributions for spin-up, spin-down, difference of these two, and non-interacting (only spin-up)

children.statement: Calculate the correctness of the model.

children.issue: The code correctly constructs transition terms between all adjacent sites.
The code correctly constructs the interaction terms between particles with different spin directions at each site, as Un_{up}n_{down}.

The code correctly constructs the potential energy term generated by the external potential field at each site. The term is $V\sum_i (i-i_{center})^2 n_i$. Here n_i is the total particle number density at site i.
The code correctly constructs the number density operators for spin up and spin down particles at each site.
The code uses DMRG to obtain the ground states of the system.
The code uses ITensors and ITensorMPS packages to calculate.
The DMRG algorithm sets the number of particles with spin up and spin down to be conserved.
The expactation values are calculated using the ground state obtained by DMRG.
The code sets the cutoff parameter to be less than (or equal to) 1e-7, i.e. cutoff <= 1e-7.
The code sets the system size L=200
The code sets the bond dimension parameter for interacting and non-interacting cases at 200. Do NOT use expressions like 10 * 2^(i-1), which will be 0 when sweep number i is large.
The code sets the nsweep parameter for interacting and non-interacting cases at least 40.
The code sets the transition term coefficient to be$t=1$
The code sets the coefficient of the interaction terms between particles to be $U/t=-800/L$ and $U=0$. Here t is the tunneling strength, and L is the system size.

The coefficient of the potential energy term (the V in front of (i-i_center)^2 n_i) is set to be 4*A/L^2 (A is merely a name, other vairable names are also acceptable). And A is set to be 6400/L^2=0.16. Thus V equals to 4*0.16/L^2, or 4*6400/L^4. Equivalent formulations/numerical values are acceptable.
The code sets the number of spin up particles to be conserved at 20 and the number of spin down particles to be conserved at 20.
